brief:
A UN administrative tribunal has disputed Israeli allegations that UNRWA used to justify dismissing Gaza staff members, raising questions about the credibility of the agency's personnel decisions, Al Jazeera English reported. The tribunal's ruling suggests the evidence presented by Israel to support the dismissals lacked sufficient substantiation.

The tribunal found fault with how UNRWA implemented terminations based on claims it could not adequately verify. The ruling marks a formal challenge to the agency's handling of staff conduct allegations in connection with Israel's claims.
dek: Tribunal raises questions about the credibility of UNRWA's decision to dismiss its staff without substantiated evidence.
title: UN tribunal challenges UNRWA's dismissal of Gaza staff over unsubstantiated allegations
